learning: If s-bend line losses fall below 1.0 and oscillation stays under about 0.35, the track width was the right lever. If oscillation rises above 0.35 on any track, reduce kp to 2.5 before moving the geometry again. If the s-bend stays at 1.0 losses with max_error at the floor and oscillation is low, the next step is an intermediate track of 0.095 or more gain.
notes: Accepts the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 change on the y 0.07 layout. kp is held at 2.8 to keep turn authority, and kd is raised to 0.50 to offset the roughly 11% higher effective gain from the narrower track.
rationale: Iteration 2 (score 433) is the best raced design. Its oval finishes 20 of 20 with max_error 0.0255, so the y 0.07 look-ahead is not adding lag. Its s-bend still goes off track in 18 of 20 trials at progress 0.64, with line_loss_events 1.05, max_error at the 0.06 m floor, and steering_oscillation 0.299. Slalom line losses fell from 1.75 (iteration 1) to 1.0. The Builder's stated trigger for narrowing the track is met: s-bend losses near 1.0, max_error at the floor, and oscillation below about 0.3. The Builder proposes wheel_track 0.09 with all other geometry unchanged, and I accept that geometry as proposed. Narrowing the track multiplies turn rate per unit wheel difference by 0.10/0.09 = 1.11, so the controller's effective steering gain rises by about 11%. I keep kp at 2.8 rather than lowering it, because turn authority is the goal here. The extra gain is the main oscillation risk (s-bend oscillation was already 0.30), so I raise kd from 0.45 to 0.50 to damp the signal rate of change. ki stays at 0.05 and base_speed at 1.5, since the oval finishes in 1.91 s with margin. Weights stay antisymmetric [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], which is valid for the unchanged 12 mm footprint at 15 mm pitch. Line loss stays last_direction so the robot keeps turning the way it was going when the tape leaves the sensors. Expected, not measured: s-bend line_loss_events below 1.0 and progress above 0.64, with steering_oscillation staying under about 0.35. The observation request covers per-track line losses, max_error and oscillation so the gain and track-width effects can be separated.
